title: Pip's Sleepy Flap
markdown:
The moon was a soft smile in the dark sky. It made the quiet water shiny. Skye the seal pup lay on the sand. The sand felt cool. Skye felt warm and sleepy. Beside Skye, Pudding the piglet snuggled close. Pudding’s little nose twitched. The cool sand felt like soft flour. A gentle breeze blew. It smelled like the sea and sweet flowers. A little wave whispered shhh on the shore. A soft sleepy sound. It made Skye feel peaceful.

“It is a peaceful night,” Skye said softly. His whiskers wiggled a little. Pudding agreed with a soft sigh. He felt cozy and safe. He loved the quiet night. He loved how the moon made everything glow. A shell nearby held a drop of water that looked like a tiny extra moon.

Skye and Pudding’s eyes felt heavy. The world felt slow and soft. Then they saw something tiny near a flower. It was Pip the little bat. Pip was not flying fast. Pip was moving a little. His little wings made a sound like soft leaves. He seemed to be trying something special. The flower nearby watched him, still as a listener.

Pip moved his wings a little. A small wiggle. He looked at the soft sand. He wiggled his wings again. Very slowly. He seemed a little unsure.

“Hello, little Pip,” whispered Skye, voice like soft waves. “What are you practising?”

Pudding wiggled his nose. “You look like you are dreaming on the wing.”

Pip made a tiny quiet squeak. He wanted to do a goodnight flap. A very soft and gentle flap. A special flap to help him sleep. But it felt a little wobbly.

“It is okay, Pip,” whispered Pudding, warm like milk. “Learning new things can feel a little wiggly.”

Skye showed Pip how to move his flippers. Not with a splash. With a slow smooth glide, like a feather on the air. “Like this. A soft movement. A peaceful movement.” He rocked once, sand whispering under him.

Pudding made tiny circles in the sand with his paws. “And a quiet breath.” He let out a soft sleepy breath. His tummy went up and down. “Just a little breath to help your wings follow.”

Pip watched them. His tiny eyes were wide. He lifted his little wings. He tried a gentle flap. Still a little wobbly. But softer. Quieter. Like a gentle wave. He tried another flap. And another. A little flutter. A gentle sway. A soft lift and fall. His flaps became smoother. Calmer. Like little breezes. He was not trying to fly high. He just wanted a sleepy goodnight flap. He felt a little more sure. The flower nodded, or perhaps the breeze did it for the flower.

Pip gave one last beautiful sleepy flap. So soft. So peaceful. It felt just right. He looked at the moon. He looked at his friends. They watched him with loving eyes. Pip yawned a tiny yawn. He stretched his small mouth. Then he tucked his wings around him like a soft blanket. He snuggled down on a moonlit leaf. The leaf was soft and cool. He felt safe and sleepy. Ready for dreams.

Skye and Pudding watched him settle. Their own eyes felt very, very heavy. The moonlight was warm and nice. The night was quiet. Soon they all drifted into sweet peaceful slumber, dreams full of soft waves, gentle breezes, and one small flap that had learned how to say goodnight.
